title: Assemble Sensor-Specific Pose Factors
summary: `global_factors(world_from_body, body_from_sensor, gps, magnetic, world_field, height, std, valid)` transforms(N,4,4) and shared(4,4),0<=N<=4096. Sensor offset/rotation known; one collocated GPS/magnetometer/barometer frame is a teaching restriction. GPS(N,3) world ENU meters, magnetic(N,3) sensor-frame field vector in microtesla, world_field(3) ENU same units. Require each magnetic norm and world_field norm>1e-9 including masked rows. Height(N) is sensor altitude meters in same ENU datum (pressure conversion already done). std(N,7) in[1e-6,1000], ordered3 GPS meters,3 unit-direction dimensionless,1 height meters; valid(N,3) GPS/magnetic/barometer availability. Predicted sensor pose Ts=Tb Tbs. Residual signs measured-minus-predicted: gps-p_s, magnetic/norm−R_s.T(world_field/norm), height-p_s,z. Return raw(N,7),whitened(N,7),cost Pythonfloat .5sum(whitened²); unavailable entire sensor block zero, all supplied values still validated. Whitening uses diagonal std, not full covariance. No calibrated field magnitude heuristic or bias estimation. Example allidentity, gps[1,2,3],mag[1,0,0],worldfield[1,0,0],height4,std1,allvalid=>raw[1,2,3,0,0,0,4],cost15. Examplebodyidentity, sensor offset[1,0,0],sensorrotationRz90, gps[1,0,0],mag[0,-2,0],field[5,0,0],height0=>allzero.
